conviction_note: The reported quarter is mostly pre-released through the monthly AUM releases. Rebuilding it from the company's own figures (Q3 average AUM about $100.5B against $99.0B in Q2, fee rate drifting about 0.3bp lower, comp guided at about 40%) gives about $155-157M of revenue against a $156.9M bar, and $0.86-0.90 adjusted EPS against a $0.91-0.92 bar that analysts were already cutting. That is a lean toward a small miss. Against it: the stock is already down 7.5% in 20 days and 21% from its high, Q3 net inflows of $1.55B beat Q2, and the name has risen after 5 of its last 7 prints, including +3.1% after a Q1 EPS miss. The call (first full outlook from the new CFO, the Q4 run-rate with exit AUM 4.5% below the Q3 average, and the pipeline) decides the reaction, and I have no sourced read on it. p_up is 48 and abs_move is 4.5 (between the 3.8% median reaction and a 6.0% third-party implied move), which gives -0.18. The findings sum to -0.40. The gap is small and both say near-zero.
bar: Q3 2026 adjusted EPS $0.91 (AAII, dated 2026-10-15, 2 analysts, 1 lowered in the last month, current-year EPS estimates -2.0% over the month: https://www.aaii.com/investingideas/article/515585-what-you-need-to-know-about-cohen--steers-incs-q3-earnings) and $0.92 EPS / $156.9M revenue (Benzinga, undated, probably set before the September AUM drop: https://www.benzinga.com/quote/CNS/earnings-forecasts). The two sources roughly agree but neither is fresh and both rest on 2-4 analysts. The company gives no quarterly guide; its 2026 expense guide (comp about 40% of revenue, G&A up mid-single digits on 2025, tax 25-26%) is from the Q2 call: https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CNS/Q22026. Because the bar is soft, findings that depend on it are kept small. print_vs_bar_pct blends revenue at about -0.7% and EPS at about -3%.
positioning_check: Short interest about 1.7M shares, 5.0 days to cover, about 3.3% of shares outstanding at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement. It was rising: 1.2M (08-31), then 1.5M (09-15), then 1.7M (09-30), about double the April low of 879K (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/cns/short-interest/). The short is building but not crowded. The sealed baseline has no skew: the front-expiry chain is unusable (open interest 3, ATM spread 141% of mid). Unusual Whales shows an implied earnings move of +/-6.04% dated 2026-10-15 (https://unusualwhales.com/stock/CNS/earnings), basis not stated, so it is only a rough guide. Tape: -4.73% over 5 days, -7.49% over 20 days, -21.35% from the 52-week high. Reaction history: 5 of 7 up, median absolute move 3.8%.

findings.finding: Rebuilt from the company's own month-end AUM releases (6/30 $100.1B, 7/31 $102.5B, 8/31 $101.0B, 9/30 $95.9B), Q3 average AUM is about $100.5B against Q2's $99.0B (+1.5%). At Q2's revenue per dollar of average AUM ($151.8M on $99.0B), plus one extra day and the fee-rate drift (58.4bp, then 58.1bp), that gives about $155-157M of adjusted revenue against a $156.9M bar. With comp at about 40% (guided), G&A up mid-single digits and a 25.5% tax rate, adjusted EPS comes to about $0.86-0.90 against a $0.91-0.92 bar, a small miss of about 3%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026: $0.85 against a $0.83 estimate (Benzinga), stock +4.42%. Q1 2026: a 'significant miss' of EPS estimates per a StockStory preview, yet the stock rose +3.14%. This name has not reliably punished small EPS misses.
findings.why_not_priced: The AUM inputs are public (monthly releases 08-10, 09-09 and 10-08), so a modelling analyst has them. The bar is the open question: Benzinga's $0.92/$156.9M looks set before the September -$5.1B market hit, and AAII shows only one downward revision in the month. If the street had fully marked to the September AUM, the bar would sit nearer $0.88-0.89. It may already be there; I cannot see a fresh consensus.
findings.independence: The AUM path comes from the company's July, August and September releases: https://finviz.com/news/380182/cohen-steers-announces-preliminary-assets-under-management-and-net-flows-for-july-2026, https://finviz.com/news/390482/cohen-steers-announces-preliminary-assets-under-management-and-net-flows-for-august-2026, https://finviz.com/news/400665/cohen-steers-announces-preliminary-assets-under-management-and-net-flows-for-september-2026. The expense guide is from the Q2 call transcript, https://earningswhispers.com/transcript/CNS/Q22026. The EPS number is my model, not a document.

findings.finding: Q4 starts from a lower run-rate. Exit AUM of $95.9B at 9/30 is about 4.5% below the Q3 average of about $100.5B, after a September in which the Fed raised rates 25bp, the 10-year closed at 5.27% and equity REITs fell 5.7% (global real estate -5.9%). Unless October recovered, Q4 revenue tracks down while comp (about 40%) and G&A (growing mid-single digits) do not shrink, so the outlook on the call is more likely margin-cautious than not.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No attributed guidance-driven reaction was sourced for CNS. The company gives annual expense guides, not quarterly revenue guides.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced. The stock is -7.5% over 20 days and -21% from its high, which is what pricing this would look like. What remains is how management frames Q4 margins and whether the 40% comp guide holds on lower revenue. I found no October REIT or AUM data to say whether the run-rate has recovered since 9/30.
findings.independence: The company's September release confirms the $5.1B market depreciation (https://finviz.com/news/400665/cohen-steers-announces-preliminary-assets-under-management-and-net-flows-for-september-2026). The macro-to-company link is therefore confirmed by the company's own AUM, but the Q4 expense response is inference.

findings.finding: Q3 net inflows sum to about $1.55B from the three monthly releases (July +$688M, August +$528M, September +$335M), above Q2's $1.3B and Q1's $0.5B. Open-end funds took in about $1.30B and closed-end about $0.20B. Inflows held positive through a September REIT sell-off, an annualised organic growth rate of about 6%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q2 2026 printed $1.3B of net inflows, then a record, and the stock rose +4.42%. Q4 2025 / Q1 2026 reactions were -4.17% and +3.14%, with smaller flows.
findings.why_not_priced: Largely priced: all three months are public. The quarterly total and the 'sixth straight quarter of inflows' headline have not been printed as one number yet. A release headlining record organic growth could steady a stock that has sold off on market beta rather than on flows.
findings.independence: Same company release series (July: https://finviz.com/news/380182/cohen-steers-announces-preliminary-assets-under-management-and-net-flows-for-july-2026). One source family, counted once.

findings.finding: Institutional flows weakened in Q3: about +$50M net (advisory +$163M, subadvisory about -$113M, including -$307M in September), against a won-but-unfunded pipeline of $1.6B at Q2, already down from $1.7B in Q1. If the pipeline update on the call shows a further decline, the institutional leg of the growth story weakens.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: On Q2, the pipeline dip from $1.7B to $1.6B came with a +4.42% reaction, so it was outweighed by open-end flows.
findings.why_not_priced: The pipeline figure is disclosed only on the call, so the market cannot see Q3's number yet. The monthly releases show subadvisory redemptions but not new awards.
findings.independence: The September subadvisory outflow (-$307M) is in the 10-08 release (https://finviz.com/news/400665/cohen-steers-announces-preliminary-assets-under-management-and-net-flows-for-september-2026). That shows flows, not the pipeline itself, so this is inference.

findings.finding: This is the first full quarter for the new CFO, Amit Muni (joined 2026-06-08; formerly CFO of CI Financial and of WisdomTree for 13 years), so the call is his first chance to restate or reset the expense framework (comp about 40%, G&A mid-single-digit growth) and possibly frame 2027. The direction is unknown. The effect is on how big the move is, not its sign.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO-transition call to compare. Interim CFO Donohue ran the October 2025 to Q1 2026 calls.
findings.why_not_priced: Nothing to price until he speaks. It raises the chance of an expense-guide change, which is why abs_move sits above the 3.8% median.

findings.finding: Into the print, the stock sits -7.5% over 20 days and -21% from its 52-week high, with short interest up about 40% over September (1.2M to 1.7M shares, 5.0 days to cover). On an in-line print, a building but uncrowded short and a beta-driven drawdown give some room for relief. CNS has risen after 5 of its last 7 prints.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Last 7 reactions: +4.42, +3.14, -4.17, +5.81, -3.80, +0.50, +3.05 (baseline). That is 5 up, with a mean of about +1.3%.
findings.why_not_priced: This is positioning, not information. It records that the sell-off has already absorbed the September AUM drop, so a print in line with the public AUM may not add new downside.
findings.independence: Baseline tape (run_up_20d -7.49%, pct_from_52w_high -21.35%) from the sealed file, a different source from the FINRA data.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with (unusable chain). The small negative lean on the bar agrees with the -7.5% 20-day run-up, so it is probably largely priced. The positioning and flow findings lean the other way, which is why p_up sits close to 50.
lessons_applied: Rule 6 (soft bar, two loosely agreeing undated or two-analyst sources): the reported-quarter miss was cut from -0.8 to -0.6.
Rule 1 / core table (finding agrees with the run-up, so largely priced): the Q4 run-rate finding was cut from -0.5 to -0.3.
Rule 5 (positioning is not information on its own): the positioning finding was cut from +0.4 to +0.3.
'Asking what the market missed generates pessimism', and the name's reaction history (sold-off EPS misses still rose): p_up moved from 47 to 48.
Unchanged: the flows (+0.5), pipeline (-0.3) and CFO (0.0) findings, and abs_move 4.5.
